items.title: Fix the 22 browser checks that fail on the live app
items.what: For each failing check (images 6, freshness 4, correction 5, navigation 6, connected 1), decide whether the check or the app is wrong, fix it, and have each group reviewed independently, so the checks guard the app again.
items.why: About 20 checks were failing on live code without anyone noticing, because nothing ran them before a release. Fable re-ran them today and 22 fail.
items.status_evidence: Images: fable/baseline-images 7189d30 has 3 check fixes and 1 app fix (a late Remove keeps focus). Freshness: fable/baseline-freshness 5470c99 has 4 check-side commits. Neither branch is reviewed or live. Correction (fable/baseline-correction), navigation and connected have no commits past eab5992.

items.title: Closing the Reader shows it is saving, and says when it can't close
items.what: Pressing × shows the Reader is saving your draft. If the close is refused (for example while an image is still being kept), it says so and leaves a working Reader with the draft and image intact. × and Escape behave the same.
items.why: Today × gives no sign while it saves, and a refused save makes × do nothing at all. It was found during the check repair, and aim-ux set the requirement.
items.status_evidence: Live web/app-session.mjs:253 still has 'catch { return false; }'. #355: 'That's in the repair'. No commit seen yet.

items.title: Every release must pass the full set of browser checks
items.what: Once the repair is done, every release runs every native browser check mode, and any failure blocks the release instead of sitting unseen.
items.why: Checks went red for days without anyone noticing. The vision says a check left red has stopped measuring.
items.status_evidence: Promised after the repair (#348, #355). bin/ has no gate script; it holds only aim-next, admin, codex-broker, runner and server.

items.title: Browser checks that pass or fail by luck
items.what: Stabilise the checks that fail only in full runs: images 'lost publication reload' and 'restoration footer touch gap', freshness 'correction C command recovery', and inline 'Ctrl commands and Undo'. Also stop counting Chrome's harmless 'Invalid InterceptionId' answer as a page error.
items.why: Random failures make release evidence noisy. InterceptionId failed one run in four and also hit aim-ux's screens run.
items.status_evidence: The images branch adds 'position a card before pressing it' and per-case storage. A grep for InterceptionId in tests/ finds no handling, and nothing addresses correction C.

items.title: Some older checks can pass without proving what they claim
items.what: Replace or strengthen the original native checks whose ordering assertion passes when the expected event is missing, and whose 'healthy again' waits also accept a deferred state.
items.why: Tony's priority is checks that see what he sees. These checks look green but prove less than they say (Fable's review of the scoped-update release).
items.status_evidence: Stated as a known limit in docs/scoped-updates-followups.md. No later change found.

items.title: 'Your journeys': checks that walk through Tony's actual day
items.what: A small set of real-browser journeys (laptop and phone, light and dark) that every release must pass: catch up after being away, read a long topic and reply, come back with Mark unread, answer what waits on you. Each step leaves a screenshot, release notes show which journeys passed, each friction Tony files becomes a step that fails before its fix, and the headline measure is how many problems Tony finds that no journey caught.
items.why: Tony asked how success will be validated. Today's misses all passed their own checks but looked wrong to him.
items.status_evidence: Proposed in #320 to start after Mark unread. Tony has not said yes or no, and work went to the check repair (#355).

items.title: A lettered 'Release pipeline' page Tony can reply to
items.what: A Notebook page at the top of every topic in the outcome. Each candidate has a permanent letter, a one-line description, who asked and a size, grouped into Now, Next and Candidates. Tony picks by replying with letters, and shipped items move to a dated Shipped list.
items.why: Tony asked how the pipeline of features and fixes is managed, and whether there is a numbered or lettered Notebook he can reply to.
items.status_evidence: #357: fable is building it and gathering every open request first, which is this inventory.

items.title: A 'Where things stand' page, and one cheap place to ask for status
items.what: One outcome Notebook page showing what's live, what's next and when, who owns what, and each journey's latest result. It is updated every release and shown at the top of every topic, so Tony can ask about status in one place without waking several agents.
items.why: Tony has to work out where to ask, and worries that asking makes several agents spend tokens.
items.status_evidence: Proposed in #320. The strip of standing references exists, but no such page has been reported. It may overlap with the Release pipeline page.

items.title: Shared understanding of the goal and how it is measured
items.what: Tony and the working agent can each state the intended result, the next useful action and the evidence that settles it. These are recorded and compared, so Tony doesn't have to read every exchange.
items.why: Tony: discussion is not shared understanding of the goal and its measure, and this is 'the big banana'.
items.status_evidence: The recording method is in the evaluation Notebook (rev 2, #240). No sample has been taken.

items.title: A reply written in the Reader records which message it answers
items.what: A reply from the Reader carries a link to the message being read, and everyone sees that link.
items.why: Tony asked whether agents can see what he is replying to without a quote. They can't: the app never records it, and only agents set the link.
items.status_evidence: Tony: 'let's track it'. In web/, reply_to appears only as a draft field (editor, cleanup, session), and nothing in the Reader sets it.

items.title: Messages show tables and formatting
items.what: Tables, lists and headings in a message render readably in the topic and the Reader, as the old AIM message view did, instead of as raw text.
items.why: Tony pastes messages into AIM to read their tables.
items.status_evidence: Message bodies render as white-space:pre-wrap plain text, and web/ has no markdown or table rendering. It is 4th on the road ahead (#193).

items.title: Every deploy posts its results to the outcome, and a regression stops it
items.what: Every deploy runs the outcome's checks and posts what passed, what failed and the timings to one shared evaluation record on the outcome. A result that got worse blocks the deploy, and a failing check opens a topic to fix it.
items.why: Tony wants evaluation to drive the work. aim-core recommended one durable record that every release updates.
items.status_evidence: The evaluation Notebook exists, but nothing updates it per release and there is no deploy gate.

items.title: Checks that measure speed, on every deploy
items.what: A small set of timing measures (how long a topic takes to open as history grows, how long a message takes to appear on its reader's page, how long test phases take) runs every release at named data sizes, so the curve is visible.
items.why: Tony: AIM failed as a platform partly because it lacked repeatable diagnostics showing speed holds as data grows. None of the current checks measure time.
items.status_evidence: Named 'the first item after this release' (#192). tests/ has only VM-step bound checks (test_*_bounds.py), with no timing suite or reporting.

items.title: Outcomes carry their target and the checks that prove it
items.what: Each outcome holds a few sentences saying what done looks like, plus its checks. Whether it is being built or kept comes from the check results, not from a type.
items.why: Tony wants the target legible to people and agents without adding new outcome or topic types.
items.status_evidence: Agreed in discussion and in VISION.md; nothing built.

items.title: An outcome's checks run on every change before it merges
items.what: An outcome's checks run before a change merges, and again at deploy.
items.why: Tony left the call to fable, who chose it: a regression caught before merging costs minutes, and one caught after deploy costs Tony.
items.status_evidence: Decided; no pre-merge runner exists.

items.title: Topics can say 'done when this check passes'; agents can close a passing outcome
items.what: A topic can name the check that finishes it, and that check then joins the outcome's standing checks. An agent may close an outcome whose checks all pass; the checks keep running and its skills stay usable.
items.why: This makes 'done' checkable rather than just declared. Tony said agents must be able to close outcomes that are truly done.
items.status_evidence: Agreed; not built.

items.title: Skills and tools have a home outcome
items.what: Each skill or tool an agent builds has a home outcome where it is improved and evaluated, and any outcome can use it. Changing a skill reruns the checks of every outcome that uses it.
items.why: Tony asked where skills and tools fit and how to keep improvements from going backwards.
items.status_evidence: Design agreed in discussion; nothing built.

items.title: Add Tony's later answers to the vision doc

notes:
I merged the three sweeps into one list of 66 items still open, in flight or unclear, ordered by value to Tony. I also checked their claims against the live code at 85fefab, read the docs, and read every message after #340 in the eight topics I can open.

**New since the sweeps**
- What's live #357 (fable to Tony): fable is building a 'Release pipeline' Notebook page with permanent letters and Now / Next / Candidates sections. This inventory feeds it. Added as in flight.
- Branch state:
  - fable/baseline-images (7189d30) holds 3 check fixes and 1 app fix (a late Remove keeps focus).
  - fable/baseline-freshness (5470c99) holds 4 check fixes.
  - fable/baseline-correction has no commits past eab5992.
  - origin/codex/aim-next is at eab5992; it includes the Notebook-click check fix and the covered-target harness change. Both are test-only.

**Code checks that settled conflicts between readers**
- Rail wrap shift: shipped. The rail scrolls on its own (a43ea6c), live by #274.
- Clearer version advice: shipped. store.py and migrations.py carry 'run code that reads version N' (fable/schema-newer-advice).
